source: full YouTube auto-caption transcript 0:00-48:55 (tools/video_draft.py transcript mqZsj4Vg2Es), card names corrected against data/Sets/FRA_PremierDraft_All_Data.json; pure game narration left out

ideas.claim: Kwia Vigorbloom is a better P1p1 than Chandra, Chill of Compliance: an evasive 6/6 with ward 2 wins unanswered, while Chandra needs protection and is easy to pressure.
ideas.quote: I think like that Kwia is a little better. Chandra like doesn't really like she kind of needs protection to do well ... and Kwia is just like giant 6/6 flyer. If they can't kill it, you win the game. So, and ward 2 makes it a little bit more resilient even if they can kill it.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR and top players' pick order (ALSA among 60%+ drafters) of the two cards; within-deck value per game in hand.

ideas.claim: Chandra, Chill of Compliance is worth less in decks that cannot protect her (few creatures / blockers).
ideas.quote: she kind of needs protection to do well and like she'll draw you a card like half the time and makes a mana some of the time and like she's kind of easy to pressure
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck in-hand value of Chandra split by the deck's creature count (pre-registered terciles).

ideas.claim: Kwia Vigorbloom ({3}{G}{W}{W}) is splashable in any white deck: its single green pip makes it a splash card for a white base.
ideas.quote: Yeah, we'll start with a Kwia. We can also just splash it in any white deck.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck in-hand value of Kwia in W-base decks splashing G (B5 design, sources seen) against its value in GW decks.

ideas.claim: Koth of the Homestead is better than Koth, the Geomancer because the counter mode matters more than the mana mode.
ideas.quote: and then I think that this Koth has been pretty nice. This Koth also does some stuff in like red, black, but I think that the counter matters a little bit more than the mana mode.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR comparison of the two cards, all decks and 60%+ players.

ideas.claim: Recursive Recruitment is a strong card; seeing it wheel at pick 9 is a sign UB is open.
ideas.quote: I also love Recursive Recruitment. very sweet card.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR in UB against ALSA; how often it wheels in 17Lands draft data.

ideas.claim: When the rare is missing from P1p2, the pack carries little signal.
ideas.quote: the rare is missing. So we don't get a huge signal point.
ideas.test_idea: not testable with public data (the card taken from the pack upstream is not in 17Lands' public draft data)

ideas.claim: Early in pack 1, a mono-coloured two-drop in the main colour beats a comparable gold card, because the gold card commits to a pair too soon.
ideas.quote: I don't necessarily want to commit to playing that color combo right after I took Kwia ... Teyo is also very good. I like getting a good two drop and it's in my main color.
ideas.test_idea: Among 60%+ drafters at P1p2-p5, rate of taking a gold card over a mono card with equal or lower GIH WR, against later picks; and their win rate when they do.

ideas.claim: Seven-drops should not be taken highly, even good ones like Archive Arbiter.
ideas.quote: I just don't love taking seven drops too highly.
ideas.test_idea: Top players' pick position of 7-drops against their GIH WR rank; deck value of a 7-drop given the deck's other 5+ drops.

ideas.claim: Campus Crier is excellent, and extra copies keep their value (they stack).
ideas.quote: I like Campus Crier a lot. ... This card's just excellent, I think, a lot of the time. Get you some surveil. You can stack it
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck in-hand value of Campus Crier in decks with 2+ copies against decks with one.

ideas.claim: Countersculpt is solid but should not be taken highly.
ideas.quote: I haven't been taking Countersculpt quite as highly. I think it's pretty solid.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of counterspells against ordinary spells, by skill group.

ideas.claim: Surgical Precision is playable but should not be prioritised, and Arcane Amphisbaena is worse than he first rated it.
ideas.quote: Surgical Precision's been okay, but I don't love prioritizing it too highly. I have moved Arcane Amphisbaena down a bit in my priority levels.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR against ALSA for both cards; within-deck value.

ideas.claim: Loot, the Nexus is valuable as ramp into big cards and as fixing for splashes.
ideas.quote: Loot, the Nexus can ramp up to my big stuff and splash.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of Loot in decks with 2+ five-plus drops or a splash, against decks without.

ideas.claim: Warrior's Blades is a card worth splashing.
ideas.quote: Warrior's Blades is pretty good. If I did want to splash, Warrior's Blades could be the pick.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck in-hand value of Warrior's Blades when splashed (B5 design, with sources seen) against its on-colour value.

ideas.claim: Ruric Thar, Biomagus overperforms; taking it keeps him off a green commitment.
ideas.quote: I also love this Ruric Thar. Kind of want to take this one honestly. It's like a card that I'm very impressed with every time I play it. Yeah, I don't want to get too committed to green.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Ruric Thar, Biomagus against its ALSA and v2's pick score (v2 had it rank 7 at P1p4).

ideas.claim: Twisted Fates is a very strong card and a fine splash for a white base (single black pip), better than an on-colour Blossom-Blessed Angel.
ideas.quote: Okay. And now we get a Twisted Fates. That's a very good card. Blossom-Blessed Angel's also good, but we can just splash the Kwia if we really need to or splash Twisted Fates
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of Twisted Fates when splashed in W-base decks against Blossom-Blessed Angel on colour.

ideas.claim: A dual land for the splash colour is worth more than an off-colour playable once the pool holds splashable bombs; fixing value rises with the number of splash cards already taken.
ideas.quote: Now, this land helps me with the Twisted Fates or with the Kwia. The blue card isn't going to get in right now
ideas.test_idea: 17Lands picks of 60%+ drafters: rate of taking a dual over a playable as a function of splash-colour cards held (pre-registered counts 0, 1, 2+); deck win rate by duals x splash cards.

ideas.claim: With no payoff in a colour yet, take the splash-worthy card before the land that would fix it.
ideas.quote: I don't have any red cards to splash other than the Warrior's Blades. So, let's take the card that's like worthy of splashing before we go too off the deep end.
ideas.test_idea: Same pick data as mqZ-16: with 0 cards of the dual's off colour, top players' rate of taking the payoff over the dual.

ideas.claim: Blessed Ghoul is only good with enchantments in the deck.
ideas.quote: Blessed Ghoul. This thing gets an enchantment. This is not an enchantment. maybe I'll find an enchantment that I really want.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of Blessed Ghoul by the deck's enchantment count.

ideas.claim: Pia, Aether Ascetic is not a good card.
ideas.quote: I just don't think Pia is very good.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR and within-deck value of Pia against its ALSA.

ideas.claim: Murmuring Volume is a weak card in general but is worth taking as fixing in a splash deck, over Fateshaper Aspirant.
ideas.quote: I don't love Murmuring Volume generally speaking, but I really don't like the Fateshaper even though I have a couple cards.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck: does Murmuring Volume in hand make a splash card castable like a land source does (B5 sensitivity).

ideas.claim: Fateshaper Aspirant is weak even with several legendaries in the pool; at best a value card to recur top-end legends, and the first cut.
ideas.quote: It's a nice little value card maybe for getting back my big top end guys.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of Fateshaper Aspirant by the deck's count of legendary creatures.

ideas.claim: Unsummon is better than Ferocity of the Hunt and better than the removal aura Infinite Coursework.
ideas.quote: an Unsummon. I like Unsummon better than Ferocity of the Hunt. ... I think Unsummon is better than Coursework.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of Unsummon against Infinite Coursework in blue decks (same decks where both are played).

ideas.claim: Gold cards of a pair flowing late signal that the pair is open less reliably than mono-coloured cards do: the pair's gold cards can be open while each colour is not.
ideas.quote: Blue black looks like it was pretty open here. Like we're seeing the charms and stuff, but it could also be the case that specifically blue black's open while blue and black are not open. Like we haven't seen any good mono black cards.
ideas.test_idea: 17Lands draft data: does late availability of a pair's gold cards predict the drafter's final pair (and its win rate) less than late availability of mono cards of the same quality?

ideas.claim: A second copy of a six-drop finisher is worth less than fixing once one copy and another top-end card are in the pool.
ideas.quote: We already have one Ruric Thar. We already have another second top end card.
ideas.test_idea: Deck-level value of the nth 5+ drop at equal quality (top-end saturation).

ideas.claim: In a deck planning several splashes, base-colour cards are the scarce resource and are worth more than splash cards of similar power.
ideas.quote: Getting a Jace is really good because that's one of our base color cards.
ideas.test_idea: Pick data: top players' rate of taking on-colour over equal-GIH splash cards as a function of splash cards held; deck win rate by on-colour depth in splash decks.

ideas.claim: Refute Destiny is narrow: it only hits green or blue creatures and planeswalkers.
ideas.quote: Creature or planeswalker that's green or blue? It's not a lot of blue creatures I want to exile. There are some green ones though.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of conditional removal against unconditional removal and ordinary spells.

ideas.claim: Restore with Empathy is a good card for a lifegain deck (regrowth plus four life).
ideas.quote: this card's pretty interesting. Like, you gain four life.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of Restore with Empathy in decks with 3+ lifegain payoffs against decks without.

ideas.claim: Jiang Yanggu, Never Alone (with its Mowu token) is a really strong card and a good single-pip splash.
ideas.quote: I think Mowu is really strong.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR and splashed in-hand value of Jiang Yanggu, Never Alone (v2 had it rank 6 at P2p2).

ideas.claim: Basic landcyclers come late; take power early and pick up landcyclers later in the pack.
ideas.quote: Let's try to get the land cyclers a bit later.
ideas.test_idea: 17Lands draft data: ALSA and wheel rate of the basic landcyclers; how often a drafter who passes one early still ends with 2.

ideas.claim: Splash only cards that are clearly above an on-colour replacement.
ideas.quote: There's another splash card. We don't want to splash unless it's extremely
ideas.test_idea: Deck value of a splash by the splash card's GIH WR edge over the deck's 23rd on-colour card.

ideas.claim: Cheap cards you want on curve (Loot, the Nexus) lose more value as splash cards than expensive ones; a splash colour should be for late-game cards.
ideas.quote: Yeah, maybe Loot because it's on the green splash isn't going to be as good and I should have just taken the tap land.
ideas.test_idea: B5 within-deck design split by the splashed card's cmc (2-3 vs 4+): the 0-source cost and the net per-card effect.

ideas.claim: The base colours are set by the double-pip cards; a colour with double-pip cards cannot be the splash.
ideas.quote: I kind of forgot that green wasn't a base color because I do have these double blue cards to to play.
ideas.test_idea: Builder check: share of top players' decks whose splash colour holds a double-pip card in their pool vs in their deck.

ideas.claim: Even a splash-heavy deck needs its early game: a mediocre on-colour two-drop is better than more fixing.
ideas.quote: I'm just going to take a two drop of blue. That'll actually be better. Want to make sure my early game is kind of
ideas.test_idea: Deck win rate by two-drop count, split by splash vs no splash.

ideas.claim: Room of Refuge is a better fixer than Murmuring Volume.
ideas.quote: Murmuring Volume or Room of Refuge. Let's take the Room of Refuge and try to get another Murmuring Volume a little bit later.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck castability of splash cards with Room of Refuge vs Murmuring Volume in hand (B5 design).

ideas.claim: Traxos, Academy Guardian is a very strong card; Jace's Machinations is only okay.
ideas.quote: Jace's Machinations is pretty okay. I love Traxos. Traxos is just a very strong card.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR against ALSA of both cards.

ideas.claim: Koth of the Homestead is especially good in a lifegain deck that wants to survive long games.
ideas.quote: Koth is also very nice in this sort of deck where you just want to gain life and just like survive for a while.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of Koth of the Homestead by the deck's lifegain card count.

ideas.claim: Mindseeker Oculus is a great pickup in a deck with planeswalker-conditional tapped lands: keeping a Jace around makes them enter untapped.
ideas.quote: I love Mindseeker Oculus. That's a perfect pickup for me, especially because it'll make these lands come into play untapped if I can keep a Jace around.
ideas.test_idea: Deck level: interaction of planeswalker-conditional duals with empower-Jace / walker count.

ideas.claim: A deck with many tapped fixing lands should play more lands (about 20) to have untapped sources when needed.
ideas.quote: I'm gonna have infinite taplands. I'm going to probably play like 20 lands in this deck or something just to make sure I have untapped sources when I need them as well.
ideas.test_idea: Deck win rate of 17 vs 18 lands by count of tapped nonbasics and splash colours.

ideas.claim: For a gold bomb, base the deck in the colour with its double pips and splash the single-pip colour (Kwia {3}{G}{W}{W}: base white, splash green).
ideas.quote: I think blue white is pretty much where I was supposed to end up just because Kwia wants me to be base white. Like white doesn't seem particularly open, but we have white like cards as like base.
ideas.test_idea: Among decks playing a gold card with uneven pips, share that splash the single-pip colour, and in-hand value when they do vs when they base it.

ideas.claim: A splash colour becomes worth it with two good cards of that colour, not one: the cost of the splash is per colour, the gain is per card.
ideas.quote: And now that I have a second one of these, I feel like splashing red will be very good at least.
ideas.test_idea: Deck level: win rate of one-colour splashes by number of splash cards (1, 2, 3+), quality controlled; or within deck, value per splash card by splash-card count.

ideas.claim: Twisted Fates is worse in this many-colour lands deck than in an ordinary deck.
ideas.quote: Twisted Fates isn't going to be as good in this deck as it would be in another
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of Twisted Fates by the deck's number of colours; reason not stated in the video.

ideas.claim: Proctor of Potential is a good WU gold card for a surveil deck.
ideas.quote: ooh, nice little blue, white, gold card. Just surveilling, set myself up.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Proctor of Potential in WU against ALSA.

ideas.claim: Your Fate Ends Here is a great removal spell.
ideas.quote: Now we get a nice little Your Fate Ends Here. Great kill spell.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR and within-deck removal value of Your Fate Ends Here.

ideas.claim: Two base colours plus one splash colour is better than splashing several colours.
ideas.quote: honestly, my blue white deck is probably better. Like, blue white just splashing green is probably the best bet.
ideas.test_idea: Deck level, all decks with skill control: win rate of 2+ splash colours vs one, at equal mean spell GIH WR (B5 dropped these 14% of splash games).

ideas.claim: Awaken the Inferno is the best of the basic landcyclers (6-damage removal); Undulating Witness is also good.
ideas.quote: Let's take Awaken the Inferno. Probably the best of the land cyclers. And the white one's pretty good, too.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR and within-deck value of the landcyclers, cast vs cycled where game data allows.

ideas.claim: Thirteen creatures is enough for a deck.
ideas.quote: I have 13 creatures, so we'll be fine on
ideas.test_idea: Deck win rate by creature count, quality controlled.

ideas.claim: Proft, Consulting Detective gets much better with many surveil effects in the deck.
ideas.quote: So, I'm going to have a decent amount to surveil. Proft is going to be great.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of Proft by count of scry/surveil cards in the deck.

ideas.claim: Fixing has diminishing returns: with about six fixing lands, take power over more fixing.
ideas.quote: I already have tons of lands. I have one, two, three, four, five, six lands. So, I'm still making some cuts to the deck for power level reasons. So, this will be a nice little power addition.
ideas.test_idea: Deck level: splash-deck win rate by count of nonbasic fixers (0-2, 3-4, 5-6, 7+), quality controlled.

ideas.claim: Arni underperforms: a creature that wants to sit back is worse than one you can trade off.
ideas.quote: I have not been that impressed with Arni, honestly, cuz I I don't I just want to play it and trade my creatures off. I don't want to have to let them sit around for a while.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of the Arni cards against ALSA.

ideas.claim: Extra copies of a splash card are worth little: with two of a splash card, a fixing land beats the third.
ideas.quote: But, we'll get the land here. We're not going to miss out on third Twisted Fates because it's already a splash card.
ideas.test_idea: Deck level: value of the nth splash card (cap on splash cards per deck).

ideas.claim: An on-colour removal spell is worth more than another splash land.
ideas.quote: This does help me splash, but I think I would like an on color kill spell.
ideas.test_idea: Deck-level removal floor: win rate below 6 removal spells, quality controlled.

ideas.claim: Six two-drops is enough; he counts two-drops as a deck-shape target.
ideas.quote: So I have one, two, three, four, five, six, two drops. If I don't play the Cryotheory Adept.
ideas.test_idea: Deck win rate by two-drop count, quality controlled.

ideas.claim: Two basic landcyclers together count as about one land.
ideas.quote: I think these two will cumulatively account for a land.
ideas.test_idea: Deck win rate of 16 vs 17 lands with 2+ landcyclers.

ideas.claim: Way of the Mind Sculptor is good card draw for the top end of a grindy deck.
ideas.quote: I like Way of the Mind Sculptor. Some card draw for the top end for the grindy
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of Way of the Mind Sculptor by deck speed (mean cmc tercile) and empower-Jace count.

ideas.claim: Icy Reception is poor in slow, grindy decks.
ideas.quote: I don't love Icy Reception in my grindier decks.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of Icy Reception by deck speed tercile (mean cmc), pre-registered.

ideas.claim: Living Library is a bad card.
ideas.quote: I just hate Living Library.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Living Library against ALSA.

ideas.claim: Protege's Awakening is strong but not for a deck that cannot protect it and already has card advantage.
ideas.quote: Protege's Awakening last pick is crazy. I feel like that card's pretty good. I'm not going to be playing it, I don't think, cuz I have my card advantage from other things.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of Protege's Awakening by the deck's count of other card-advantage cards.

ideas.claim: A third splash colour carried by two cards (Twisted Fates) is not worth it.
ideas.quote: I probably shouldn't be splashing black, but we will anyway.
ideas.test_idea: Same deck-level test as mqZ-44, with the number of cards per splash colour.

ideas.claim: With enough turn-two plays, cut the weaker cheap cards (Surveillance Phantasm, Cryotheory Adept) before top end.
ideas.quote: And then we have all these things to do on turn two. So, I cut one Vinelasher
ideas.test_idea: Deck win rate by two-drop count above the pair's median, quality controlled.

ideas.claim: Count splash sources with non-land fixers (landcyclers, Murmuring Volume) as part sources: 7 blue, 7 white, 'kind of' 3 black, 4 red, 6 green.
ideas.quote: So I have five, six, seven blue sources. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven white sources. One, two, kind of three black sources. One, two, three, kind of four red One, two, three, four, five, six green sources kind of.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck castability of splash cards by land sources vs non-land sources seen.

ideas.claim: Cut double-pip cards of a splash colour; a deck splashing green should not play its only GG card.
ideas.quote: Um, let's just cut our only double green card. That makes our mana a little bit more consistent.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of double-pip splash cards by sources seen.

ideas.claim: Cutting the deck's only on-colour removal spell (Infinite Coursework) for a landcycler creature is a risky cut.
ideas.quote: Let's just cut Infinite Coursework or Our on-colour removal spell, which is probably a dicey cut.
ideas.test_idea: Deck-level removal floor (as mqZ-51).

ideas.claim: Keep a hand missing a splash colour when it holds a fixer that will find it.
ideas.quote: Okay, we'll keep it. ... We're going to get white mana with this. We are just missing green, but this will get us our green
ideas.test_idea: Opening-hand data: kept 7s with 0 splash-colour lands, with vs without a fixer in hand, within deck.

ideas.claim: Unsummon pairs with Twisted Fates and a big threat: bounce a blocker, land the threat, then kill the bounced card when it comes back.
ideas.quote: I'm just going to hold back and use Unsummon here probably and then I'll play Ruric Thar and then I will use Twisted Fates on whatever I unsummoned most likely.
ideas.test_idea: not testable with public data (sequencing is not in 17Lands' public game data)

ideas.claim: Reality Fracture supports four- and five-colour decks: opponents also play many extra lands.
ideas.quote: They're also playing a crazy number of extra lands, which is really funny. The four-color deck versus the five-color
ideas.test_idea: Share of decks with 3+ colours and their win rate at equal quality, all players and 60%+.

ideas.claim: Basic landcyclers are poor fixing beyond one or two per deck; about two is the right number.
ideas.quote: I feel like the land cyclers are actually not that good for fixing like having more than like one or two maybe.
ideas.test_idea: Deck level: splash-deck win rate by landcycler count (0, 1, 2, 3+), quality controlled; within deck, splash castability with a landcycler as the only source.

ideas.claim: Murmuring Volume (the mana rock) carried the five-colour mana in a game.
ideas.quote: I feel like I was pretty happy having like the five-color stuff and the the the mana rock thing definitely carried me a bit.
ideas.test_idea: Within-deck value of Murmuring Volume in decks with 2+ splash colours vs one or none.

ideas.claim: Multi-colour splashes leave the deck missing colours even with many fixing lands; many tapped lands slow it down.
ideas.quote: If we're playing all these lands, then we still won't have all our colors. This is why splashing multiple colors is tough.
ideas.test_idea: Within deck (B5 design extended to multi-colour splashes): rate of splash cards stuck in hand by number of splash colours.

ideas.claim: Enters-tapped lands cost tempo; playing many of them is bad.
ideas.quote: We have all our colors. It's just playing all these tap lands is definitely bad.
ideas.test_idea: Deck level: win rate per on-colour tapped land and for 4+ tapped lands, quality controlled.

ideas.claim: With two bombs, lead with the one that demands an answer so the other survives; bombs protect each other.
ideas.quote: Yeah, let's try to get Ruric Thar down first. None of their creatures are particularly scary, and Ruric Thar is going to be a huge issue. or at least demand an answer from them.
ideas.test_idea: Within deck: in-hand value of a top-10 card when a second top-10 card is also in hand, against alone.

ideas.claim: A multi-splash deck works when its early game is all base colours, so opening hands are castable without the splash.
ideas.quote: We have nice early game. I mean that game we literally drew I think one, two, like all of our early game cards that were just blue and white. Like like our opening hand was just like a blue white hand.
ideas.test_idea: Same split as mqZ-31: splash cards by cmc; and deck win rate of splash decks by share of cmc <= 3 spells that are off-colour.

ideas.claim: Two basic landcyclers is a good number for a multi-splash deck.
ideas.quote: We have a couple of land cycles. I think like two is probably a good number.
ideas.test_idea: As mqZ-66: deck win rate by landcycler count in splash decks.
